You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

===== documents/matters/1006-00005/Settlement/settlement-agreement-and-mutual-release.docx =====

**WHEREAS**, on or about June 7, 2021, CPS filed a lawsuit styled *Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC v. Ridgeway Freight Services Inc.*, Cause No. 342-2021-04871-TX, in the 342nd Judicial District Court of Tarrant County, Texas (the \"Lawsuit\"), asserting claims for breach of contract, money had and received, common-law fraud, and unjust enrichment, and seeking recovery of One Million Eight Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand Six Hundred Thirty-Two Dollars and Nineteen Cents (\$1,847,632.19) in alleged overcharges, together with contractual interest, attorneys\' fees, costs of court, and exemplary damages;

**WHEREAS**, Ridgeway filed a counterclaim in the Lawsuit asserting breach of contract based on CPS\'s alleged wrongful termination of the MTSA, seeking recovery of Three Hundred Forty Thousand Dollars (\$340,000.00) in alleged lost profits and related consequential damages;

--

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Settlement Amount**

Ridgeway shall pay to CPS the total sum of One Million Five Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$1,575,000.00) (the \"Settlement Amount\"), subject to and in accordance with the payment schedule set forth below:

> **(a) First Installment.** One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000.00) shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., no later than January 2, 2022). Such payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated in writing by CPS in accordance with Section 1.3 below.
>
> **(b) Second Installment.** Five Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$575,000.00) shall be due and payable within ninety (90) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., no later than March 3, 2022). Such payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated in writing by CPS in accordance with Section 1.3 below.

The Settlement Amount shall be allocated and reported for tax purposes in accordance with applicable law, and each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations arising from or relating to the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount. Neither Party makes any representation or warranty to the other regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Amount or any portion thereof.

**Section 1.2 --- Late Payment**

In the event that Ridgeway fails to make any installment payment when due as set forth in Section 1.1, interest shall accrue on the unpaid amount at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (eighteen percent (18%) per annum) from the applicable due date until such payment, together with all accrued interest thereon, is paid in full. Such interest shall compound monthly on the last calendar day of each month.

Upon any payment default by Ridgeway that remains uncured for ten (10) business days following written notice of such default from CPS to Ridgeway in accordance with Section 7.8, CPS shall be entitled, at its sole option and in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, to enter a consent judgment against Ridgeway in the amount of the entire unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, plus all accrued and unpaid interest thereon, plus CPS\'s reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs incurred in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement (collectively, the \"Judgment Amount\"). Ridgeway hereby irrevocably consents to the entry of such judgment in the 342nd Judicial District Court of Tarrant County, Texas, and irrevocably waives any objection to personal jurisdiction, subject-matter jurisdiction, or venue in connection therewith. The Parties acknowledge that this consent judgment provision is a material inducement to CPS\'s agreement to accept installment payments rather than a single lump-sum payment, and that the enforcement rights set forth in this Section 1.2 are reasonable and necessary to protect CPS\'s legitimate interests under this Agreement.

--

Effective upon CPS\'s receipt of the full Settlement Amount (including both the First Installment and the Second Installment as set forth in Section 1.1), CPS, on behalf of itself and its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"CPS Releasing Parties\"), hereby fully, finally, unconditionally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges Ridgeway and its shareholders, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates, insurers, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Ridgeway Released Parties\") from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, judgments, executions, obligations, damages, losses, costs, expenses, and liabilities of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether arising under statute, contract, tort, or otherwise, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, liquidated or unliquidated, that the CPS Releasing Parties ever had, now have, or hereafter may have against the Ridgeway Released Parties, from the beginning of the world through the Effective Date, arising out of, relating to, or in any way connected with: (i) the MTSA, including all amendments, schedules, and addenda thereto; (ii) the Lawsuit, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and defenses asserted or that could have been asserted therein; or (iii) the transactions, services, invoices, payments, disputes, negotiations, communications, and events described in or relating to the MTSA or the Lawsuit.

--

Effective as of the Effective Date, Ridgeway, on behalf of itself and its shareholders, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates, insurers, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Ridgeway Releasing Parties\"), hereby fully, finally, unconditionally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges CPS and its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"CPS Released Parties\") from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, judgments, executions, obligations, damages, losses, costs, expenses, and liabilities of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether arising under statute, contract, tort, or otherwise, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, liquidated or unliquidated, that the Ridgeway Releasing Parties ever had, now have, or hereafter may have against the CPS Released Parties, from the beginning of the world through the Effective Date, arising out of, relating to, or in any way connected with: (i) the MTSA, including all amendments, schedules, and addenda thereto; (ii) the Lawsuit, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and defenses asserted or that could have been asserted therein; or (iii) the transactions, services, invoices, payments, disputes, negotiations, communications, and events described in or relating to the MTSA or the Lawsuit. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the release set forth in this Section 2.2 specifically encompasses and includes Ridgeway\'s counterclaim for alleged lost profits of Three Hundred Forty Thousand Dollars (\$340,000.00) and any and all other claims for damages, whether direct, indirect, consequential, incidental, special, punitive, or exemplary, arising from or related to CPS\'s termination of the MTSA.

The Parties acknowledge and agree that Ridgeway\'s release under this Section 2.2 is effective immediately upon the Effective Date and is not conditioned upon CPS\'s receipt of the Settlement Amount or any installment thereof.

--

The Parties agree that the existence and terms of this Agreement, including without limitation the Settlement Amount and the payment schedule, are and shall remain strictly confidential. Except as expressly provided in this Section 4.1, neither Party shall disclose, publicize, or disseminate, directly or indirectly, the terms, conditions, or substance of this Agreement to any third party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may disclose the terms of this Agreement:

**NOW, THEREFORE,** in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

--

\(j\) \"**Settlement Payment**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.1 of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 Payment by Vantage.** In consideration of the mutual releases and other covenants contained herein, Vantage shall pay to Meridian a lump-sum settlement payment in the amount of One Million Nine Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$1,950,000.00) (the \"Settlement Payment\"). The Settlement Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States dollars to the account designated by Meridian in writing in accordance with the wire transfer instructions set forth on Exhibit A attached hereto. The Settlement Payment shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days following the Effective Date (i.e., no later than November 27, 2022). In the event that November 27, 2022, falls on a day that is not a business day, the Settlement Payment shall be due on the next succeeding business day.

**Section 2.2 Characterization of Payment.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that the Settlement Payment constitutes a one-time quality accommodation payment made by Vantage in the interest of resolving the disputed Chargebacks and preserving the ongoing commercial relationship between the Parties under the LTSA. The Settlement Payment does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, fault, defect, or wrongdoing by Vantage or any of its affiliates with respect to the Parts, the field failures in MPT-8AT transmissions, or any other matter. The Settlement Payment is not intended to, and shall not, establish a precedent for the resolution, valuation, or payment of any future warranty claims, chargebacks, or disputes arising under the LTSA or any other agreement between the Parties.

**Section 2.3 Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own federal, state, local, and foreign tax obligations, if any, arising from or attributable to the Settlement Payment, including the obligation to report such payment to the applicable taxing authorities. No withholding shall be applied to the Settlement Payment by Vantage unless withholding is required by applicable law, in which case Vantage shall provide Meridian with prompt written notice of any such withholding and shall remit the withheld amount to the appropriate taxing authority in accordance with applicable law. Each Party agrees to provide such tax forms, certifications, or documentation as may be reasonably requested by the other Party in connection with the Settlement Payment.

--

**Section 3.1 Reversal and Restoration of Chargebacks.** Within ten (10) business days following Meridian\'s receipt and confirmation of the Settlement Payment in immediately available funds, Meridian shall reverse the full remaining balance of previously withheld Chargebacks in the aggregate amount of Two Million Nine Hundred Twenty Thousand Five Hundred Fifty Dollars and Twenty Cents (\$2,920,550.20). Such amount represents the difference between the aggregate Chargebacks of Four Million Eight Hundred Seventy Thousand Five Hundred Fifty Dollars and Twenty Cents (\$4,870,550.20) and the Settlement Payment of One Million Nine Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$1,950,000.00). Meridian shall restore such reversed amounts to Vantage\'s accounts receivable and shall issue appropriate credit memoranda, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit B, reflecting such reversals. The IRS\'s secondary argument --- that the \$312 million PCT payment undervalued the pre-existing IP portfolio --- requires direct rebuttal, even though it relates to a transaction that occurred in 2012, outside the examination years.
The IRS\'s \$852 million PCT valuation relies on Dr. Alan Washburne\'s income method / Discounted cash flow (\"DCF\") analysis using a weighted average cost of capital of 7.2%. This discount rate is inappropriately low for a pharmaceutical IP portfolio at PBI\'s stage of development. A 7.2% WACC would be appropriate for the overall cost of capital of a large, diversified, mature pharmaceutical company with a portfolio of approved, commercialized products and predictable cash flows. It is not appropriate for valuing a specific IP portfolio that, as of July 2012, included clinical-stage compounds subject to significant regulatory approval risk, market-entry risk in multiple international territories, and pipeline attrition risk inherent in pharmaceutical development.
Dr. Helena Vasquez and Dr. Rohan Chakrabarti of Whitmore Valuation Group LLC conducted an independent income method / DCF analysis of the pre-existing IP portfolio using a WACC of 9.8%. This discount rate was derived using standard cost-of-capital methodology with pharmaceutical-industry betas, adjusted for company-specific risk factors including the clinical-stage profile of certain compounds and the geographic market-entry risks associated with PBI\'s non-Americas territory. The 9.8% WACC reflects appropriate risk premiums for pharmaceutical IP, including regulatory risk, market-entry risk, and pipeline attrition. The Whitmore analysis yields an arm\'s-length range of \$278 million to \$361 million for the PCT. The \$312 million lump-sum payment made by PBI falls squarely within this arm\'s-length range, at approximately the midpoint.
Even accepting the IRS\'s own DCF methodology and revenue projections but correcting the discount rate from 7.2% to 9.8%, the resulting PCT valuation falls well below \$852 million, substantially narrowing the gap and demonstrating that the discount rate is the primary driver of the difference. The sensitivity analysis is documented in Dr. Vasquez\'s rebuttal memorandum, which was submitted as part of the Formal Protest.

The legacy compound portfolio generated \$814.6 million in non-Americas net sales in 2017, declining to \$624.1 million by 2020 --- a 23.4% decline over four years. This trajectory reflects the natural lifecycle of mature pharmaceutical products facing patent expirations and increasing generic competition. As the economic value of the licensed IP diminishes over time, the appropriate arm\'s-length royalty rate declines correspondingly, or at minimum remains stable. A royalty rate of 4.5% on a declining revenue base is entirely consistent with arm\'s-length pricing. If anything, the declining trajectory further supports a rate at or below the median, not an increase to 11.0%.
===== documents/matters/1018-00009/Appeals/appeals-pre-conference-memo.docx =====
Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. (\"PPC\") is challenging \$380.4 million in net proposed adjustments across tax years 2017 through 2020, arising from the Internal Revenue Service\'s challenge to PPC\'s transfer pricing methodology for its Irish intellectual property holding structure. The adjustments were proposed in a Notice of Proposed Adjustment (\"NOPA\") issued October 12, 2023, and formalized in a 30-Day Letter issued November 8, 2023. The IRS\'s adjustments target three interrelated areas: (1) cost-sharing ratios under the qualified cost-sharing arrangement (\"CSA\") between PPC and its Irish subsidiary, Penterra Biopharma International DAC (\"PBI\"); (2) the royalty rate charged under a legacy IP license agreement between PPC and PBI; and (3) the adequacy of the platform contribution transaction (\"PCT\") payment made by PBI to PPC at the inception of the CSA in 2012. The IRS has also raised a secondary economic substance challenge to PBI\'s role as an IP-holding company and CSA participant.
Our settlement target is resolution at 10--15% of the \$380.4 million proposed adjustment, which corresponds to a range of \$38.0 million to \$57.1 million, with a hard ceiling of 20% (\$76.1 million), as discussed and approved in the Settlement Authority Memorandum dated December 10, 2023. This settlement posture is supported by our assessment in the Hazards of Litigation Memorandum dated December 5, 2023, in which we concluded that the IRS faces significant hazards on all three primary issues, with probability-weighted downside exposure to PPC estimated at 10--18% of the proposed adjustment.
The **PCT payment** was a lump-sum payment of \$312 million paid by PBI to PPC on July 1, 2012, representing the buy-in to pre-existing intellectual property, which at that time consisted primarily of clinical-stage and approved oncology compounds, including the foundational IP for Veritaxol and certain precursor compounds. The PCT was valued using a discounted cash flow (\"DCF\") methodology at a weighted average cost of capital (\"WACC\") of 9.8%, as documented in a contemporaneous valuation report prepared by Crestfield & Associates LLP.

PPC\'s Formal Protest contests the applicability of this penalty and asserts that PPC is entitled to penalty protection under IRC § 6662(e)(3)(B) on the basis of its contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, the reasonableness of its transfer pricing methodology, and the existence of reasonable cause and good faith.
> 6\. **Dr. Helena Vasquez**, Managing Director, Whitmore Valuation Group LLC --- Dr. Vasquez is the independent economic expert retained by PPC under a Kovel arrangement (Kovel Letter Reference 1018-00009-KV, executed June 20, 2022, pursuant to *United States v. Kovel*, 296 F.2d 918 (2d Cir. 1961)). Dr. Vasquez is prepared to present and respond to questions concerning the economic analyses supporting PPC\'s transfer pricing positions, including the comparable uncontrolled transaction (\"CUT\") analysis supporting the 4.5% legacy IP royalty rate, the comparable profits method / transactional net margin method (\"CPM/TNMM\") analysis used to corroborate the arm\'s-length results of the intercompany transactions, and the platform contribution transaction (\"PCT\") valuation (income method / Discounted cash flow approach) supporting the \$312 million PCT payment made at the inception of the CSA.
> 4\. **PCT Payment Valuation.** The validity of the \$312 million platform contribution transaction payment made by PBI at the inception of the CSA. PPC\'s income method / Discounted cash flow (\"DCF\") analysis, conducted at a weighted average cost of capital (\"WACC\") of 9.8%, determined that the arm\'s-length range for the PCT payment was \$278 million to \$361 million. The actual PCT payment of \$312 million falls within this range and is therefore consistent with the arm\'s-length standard under Treasury Regulation § 1.482-7(g).

On October 12, 2023, the IRS examination team issued a Notice of Proposed Adjustment (\"NOPA\") proposing net adjustments totaling \$380,400,000 across all four tax years. In addition, the IRS proposed the imposition of a twenty percent (20%) substantial valuation misstatement penalty under IRC § 6662(e) on the underpayment of tax attributable to the proposed transfer pricing adjustments. The total agreed-upon adjustment under the settlement is **\$47,600,000** across all four tax years under examination (2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020). This settlement amount represents approximately 12.51% of the \$380,400,000 net proposed adjustment originally set forth in the NOPA. Based on the agreed-upon adjustment of \$47,600,000, PPC estimates that the resulting additional federal income tax liability will be approximately **\$10,000,000** (rounded). This estimate reflects the application of the 21% corporate income tax rate enacted by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, which is applicable to tax years 2018, 2019, and 2020, as well as the blended effective rate applied to the 2017 tax year adjustment.
PPC understands that statutory interest will be computed on the resulting underpayment at the applicable federal underpayment rate under IRC § 6621 from the respective original due dates of each return through the date of payment. Based on PPC\'s preliminary calculations, the Company estimates that such accrued interest will be approximately **\$2,840,000**, although PPC acknowledges that the final interest computation will be determined by the IRS and may differ from this estimate depending on the actual date of payment.
PPC understands and accepts that the settlement provides for the **full abatement** of the proposed IRC § 6662(e) substantial valuation misstatement penalty, which was originally proposed at approximately \$15,977,000. The abatement of the penalty reflects Appeals\' acceptance of PPC\'s reasonable-cause defense under IRC § 6664(c) and, specifically, Appeals\' recognition that PPC maintained contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation that met the requirements of IRC § 6662(e)(3)(B) and the applicable Treasury Regulations.
**Payment of Tax and Interest.** PPC will remit payment of the additional federal income tax due, estimated at approximately \$10,000,000, together with all accrued statutory interest, upon receipt of the formal assessment notice from the IRS, or at such earlier time as may be directed by Appeals. **Date of Execution: March 29, 2024**

This Closing Agreement is entered into between the taxpayer identified below and the Commissioner of Internal Revenue (the \"Commissioner\"), acting through the Commissioner\'s duly authorized representative, pursuant to the authority granted under Section 7121 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\" or \"IRC\"), and the regulations promulgated thereunder. This agreement is final and conclusive as to the specific matters covered herein, and, except upon a showing of fraud, malfeasance, or misrepresentation of a material fact, the matters agreed to herein shall not be reopened or modified by either party.

**[PART I --- IDENTIFICATION OF TAXPAYER]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Taxpayer Information**

The taxpayer that is a party to this Closing Agreement is identified as follows:

**Full Legal Name:** Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp.
--
**State of Incorporation:** Delaware

**Stock Exchange Listing:** The common stock of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. is listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"PPCA.\" As a publicly traded corporation, the taxpayer is subject to periodic reporting requirements under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended.

**Fiscal Year-End:** December 31 (calendar year taxpayer)

**Federal Income Tax Returns at Issue:** The federal income tax returns that are the subject of this Closing Agreement are the following United States Corporation Income Tax Returns (Forms 1120) filed by the taxpayer for the taxable years ending:

> \(a\) December 31, 2017;
--
All such returns were timely filed with the Internal Revenue Service.

**Section 1.2 --- Authorized Representative of the Taxpayer**

The taxpayer is represented in the execution of this Closing Agreement by the following duly authorized officer:

**Name:** Marcus Whitfield

**Title:** Vice President, Global Tax

**Authority:** Mr. Whitfield is a duly authorized officer of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. and has been vested with full authority, by resolution of the Board of Directors of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. adopted on June 1, 2022, to execute this Closing Agreement and any and all ancillary documents on behalf of the taxpayer in connection with the examination described herein.

**Address:**
--
> **Lead Revenue Agent:** Patricia Dunleavy

Following the issuance of the 30-Day Letter and the filing of a Formal Protest by the taxpayer, jurisdiction over the case was transferred from the LB&I examination team to the IRS Independent Office of Appeals, where the case was assigned to Appeals Officer Noreen Castañeda.

**Section 1.4 --- Taxpayer\'s Authorized Legal Representatives**

Throughout the examination and Appeals proceedings, the taxpayer has been represented by the following law firm, as authorized by IRS Form 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative) filed with the Internal Revenue Service on June 8, 2022:

**Firm:** Calderwood & Harkness LLP
--
**Section 2.1 --- Examination History**

On May 16, 2022, the Internal Revenue Service opened an examination of the federal income tax returns (Forms 1120) of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. for the taxable years ending December 31, 2017, December 31, 2018, December 31, 2019, and December 31, 2020. The examination was initiated by issuance of Letter 2205-A (Notification of Examination) addressed to the taxpayer at its principal place of business.

The examination was conducted by the IRS Large Business & International Division, Northeast Transfer Pricing Practice, under Exam Team ID LB&I-NE-TP-2022-00641. The examination team was led by Supervisory Revenue Agent Gerald Meskill, serving as Team Manager, and Lead Revenue Agent Patricia Dunleavy.

During the course of the examination, a total of forty-seven (47) Information Document Requests (\"IDRs\") were issued to the taxpayer between June 2022 and September 2023. The taxpayer responded to all IDRs in a timely and cooperative manner, producing documents, data, and analyses as requested by the examination team.

The examination focused principally on the transfer pricing methodology employed by the taxpayer in connection with intercompany transactions between Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. (the United States parent corporation) and its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, Penterra Biopharma International DAC (\"PBI\"). PBI is a Designated Activity Company organized under the laws of Ireland, with its registered office located at 4th Floor, Claremont House, Sandyford Business Park, Dublin D18 K7T4, Ireland. PBI\'s Irish Tax Reference Number is 3218764T.

PBI is owned one hundred percent (100%) by Penterra Holdings Luxembourg S.à r.l. (\"PHL\"), a société à responsabilité limitée organized under the laws of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, with its registered office at 14, rue Aldringen, L-1118 Luxembourg, and registered with the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés under RCS Number B 168452. PHL is itself owned one hundred percent (100%) by the taxpayer, Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. For United States federal income tax purposes, PHL has elected to be, and is treated as, a disregarded entity pursuant to Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3, such that PBI is treated as a direct subsidiary of the taxpayer for purposes of the transfer pricing rules of IRC § 482 and the regulations thereunder.

**Section 2.2 --- Intercompany Arrangements at Issue**

The examination identified and focused upon the following intercompany arrangements between the taxpayer and PBI:

**(a) Qualified Cost-Sharing Arrangement.** The taxpayer and PBI entered into a Qualified Cost-Sharing Arrangement (\"CSA\"), effective July 1, 2012, pursuant to Treasury Regulations § 1.482-7. Under the terms of the CSA, PBI acquired the right to develop and exploit certain pharmaceutical intellectual property outside of the Americas (defined in the CSA as North America, Central America, South America, and the Caribbean) in exchange for the following consideration:

> \(i\) A platform contribution transaction (\"PCT\") payment in the amount of Three Hundred Twelve Million Dollars (\$312,000,000), which was paid by PBI to the taxpayer in the taxable year ending December 31, 2012; and
>
> \(ii\) Ongoing cost-sharing payments, allocated between the taxpayer and PBI on a periodic basis in proportion to reasonably anticipated benefits (\"RAB\"), as required by Treasury Regulations § 1.482-7(d)(1).

The CSA governed the sharing of qualified research and development costs incurred in connection with the development of pharmaceutical compounds and related intangible property for the taxable years at issue.

**(b) Intercompany License Agreement for Legacy Compounds.** In addition to the CSA, the taxpayer and PBI entered into an intercompany license agreement governing the use and exploitation of legacy pharmaceutical compounds --- that is, compounds whose development was substantially completed prior to July 1, 2012 and which were therefore not covered by the CSA. Under this license agreement, PBI was granted a non-exclusive license to use, manufacture (or have manufactured), market, distribute, and sell the legacy compounds in the non-Americas territory. In consideration for this license, PBI paid the taxpayer arm\'s-length royalties calculated at a rate of four and one-half percent (4.5%) of net sales of the licensed legacy compounds in the non-Americas territory.

**Section 2.3 --- Notice of Proposed Adjustment**

On October 12, 2023, following the completion of its analysis, the IRS examination team issued a Notice of Proposed Adjustment (\"NOPA\") for all four taxable years at issue. The NOPA proposed the following adjustments to the taxpayer\'s taxable income under IRC § 482:

**(a) CSA Cost-Sharing Ratio Adjustments.** The examination team proposed an increase in PBI\'s cost-sharing percentage under the CSA, which would result in additional income allocable to the taxpayer. Specifically, the examination team contended that PBI\'s share of reasonably anticipated benefits --- and therefore its required cost-sharing contribution --- was understated by the taxpayer. The proposed adjustments were as follows:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Taxable Year**   **Taxpayer\'s Reported PBI Share**   **IRS Proposed PBI Share**   **Proposed Additional Income to Taxpayer**
  ------------------ ------------------------------------ ---------------------------- --------------------------------------------
  2017               38.2%                                48.2%                        \$48,730,000
--
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**(b) Royalty Rate Adjustments.** The examination team also proposed an increase in the royalty rate applicable to the intercompany license of legacy intellectual property from the taxpayer to PBI, from the reported rate of 4.5% of non-Americas net sales to a proposed rate of 11.0% of non-Americas net sales. The examination team asserted that comparable uncontrolled transactions and other transfer pricing methods supported a higher arm\'s-length royalty rate. The proposed adjustments were as follows:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Taxable Year**       **Non-Americas Legacy Net Sales**   **Reported Royalty Rate**   **Proposed Royalty Rate**   **Proposed Additional Income to Taxpayer**
  ---------------------- ----------------------------------- --------------------------- --------------------------- --------------------------------------------
  2017                   \$814,600,000                       4.5%                        11.0%                       \$52,949,000
--
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**(c) Correlative Offset.** The IRS allowed a correlative offset in the amount of (\$42,650,000) across all four taxable years to prevent double-counting of income attributable to the overlap between the CSA cost-sharing adjustments and the royalty rate adjustments.

**(d) Net Proposed Adjustment.** The net proposed adjustment across all four taxable years, after application of the correlative offset, was as follows:

> CSA Cost-Sharing Adjustments: \$235,010,000
>
> Royalty Rate Adjustments: \$188,040,000
>
> Less: Correlative Offset: (\$42,650,000)
>
> **Net Proposed Adjustment (All Years): \$380,400,000**

**(e) Penalty.** In addition to the proposed income adjustments, the IRS proposed a substantial valuation misstatement penalty under IRC § 6662(e) at a rate of twenty percent (20%) of the underpayment of tax attributable to the IRC § 482 allocation. The proposed penalty was calculated as follows:

> Net Proposed Adjustment: \$380,400,000
>
> Applicable Corporate Tax Rate: 21%
>
> Estimated Underpayment: \$380,400,000 × 21% = \$79,884,000
>
> Penalty (20% of Underpayment): \$79,884,000 × 20% = \$15,976,800 (approximately \$15,977,000, rounded to approximately \$15,980,000 in the NOPA)

**Section 2.4 --- 30-Day Letter and Formal Protest**

Following the issuance of the NOPA, a 30-Day Letter was issued by the IRS to the taxpayer on November 8, 2023, advising the taxpayer of its right to file a written protest and to request a conference with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.

**[Section 1: SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**
**1.1 Payment Amount and Schedule.** As settlement consideration for the claims asserted by Fonseca against the Rennick Parties, Rennick shall pay, or cause to be paid, to Fonseca the aggregate sum of Nine Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$975,000) (the \"Settlement Amount\"), payable in two installments as follows:
> **(a) First Installment.** Six Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$600,000), payable by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated by Fonseca in writing to Rennick or his counsel no later than five (5) business days after the Effective Date. The First Installment shall be due and payable within fifteen (15) business days of the Effective Date (the \"First Installment Due Date\"). The Parties acknowledge that, based on the Effective Date of July 14, 2023, and excluding weekends and federal bank holidays, the First Installment Due Date falls on August 4, 2023.
> **(b) Second Installment.** Three Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$375,000), payable by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the same bank account designated by Fonseca pursuant to Section 1.1(a) above, on or before October 15, 2023 (the \"Second Installment Due Date\").
**1.2 Late Payment.** In the event that any installment of the Settlement Amount is not received by Fonseca on or before its applicable Installment Due Date, the unpaid amount shall bear interest at the rate of ten percent (10%) per annum, calculated on a simple interest basis from the applicable Installment Due Date through and including the date of actual receipt of such payment by Fonseca. The accrual of interest under this Section 1.2 shall not limit or waive any other rights or remedies available to Fonseca under this Agreement, at law, or in equity, including the right to seek enforcement of this Agreement pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 664.6 as contemplated by Section 7.1 hereof.
**1.3 Source of Funds.** The Settlement Amount shall be the personal obligation of Rennick individually and shall not be paid, directly or indirectly, from the funds, accounts, assets, or revenues of CMP. Rennick represents and warrants that he has sufficient personal financial resources and liquidity to satisfy the Settlement Amount in accordance with the payment schedule set forth in Section 1.1 above. Nothing in this Section 1.3 shall prohibit Rennick from using funds distributed to him by CMP in the ordinary course of business in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and the Restated Waterfall (as defined below), provided that no CMP distribution shall be accelerated, preferentially directed, or otherwise manipulated for the purpose of funding the Settlement Amount.
> **(a)** During such period, CMP paid to RSV management fees in the aggregate amount of Two Million Six Hundred Ninety-Four Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$2,694,500) for management, administrative, and overhead services rendered by RSV to CMP in connection with the production, marketing, and distribution of CMP\'s feature-film properties.
> **(b)** Under Section 6.2 of the Partnership Agreement, management fees payable by CMP to any entity owned or controlled by a partner were subject to a cap of five percent (5%) of CMP\'s aggregate gross receipts. Based on aggregate gross receipts of Twenty-Three Million Two Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$23,220,000) through the second quarter of 2022, the permissible aggregate amount of such management fees was One Million One Hundred Sixty-One Thousand Dollars (\$1,161,000). The management fees actually paid to RSV therefore exceeded the permissible amount by One Million Five Hundred Thirty-Three Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$1,533,500) (the \"Excess Fees\").
> **(c)** The payment by Rennick of the Settlement Amount in accordance with Section 1 of this Agreement shall constitute full and complete satisfaction, settlement, and resolution of any and all claims, demands, causes of action, and liabilities that Fonseca or CMP may have against Rennick, RSV, or any of their respective affiliates, arising from, relating to, or in connection with the Excess Fees, including without limitation claims for breach of the Partnership Agreement, breach of fiduciary duty, unjust enrichment, conversion, accounting, constructive trust, disgorgement, or any other legal or equitable theory.
> **(d)** Upon Fonseca\'s receipt of the Settlement Amount in full, no further clawback, restitution, repayment, refund, offset, credit, or other remedy of any kind shall be required of or available against Rennick, RSV, or any of their respective affiliates with respect to the Excess Fees. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section 3 does not release or waive any rights of Fonseca with respect to management fees paid or payable by CMP on or after January 1, 2023, which shall be governed exclusively by the Restated Waterfall and Section 10 of this Agreement.
**4.1 Restoration to Distributable Profit Pool.** The Parties acknowledge that the aggregate sum of Eight Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$847,200) in domestic distribution revenues received by CMP was reclassified on CMP\'s books and records as recoupable advance repayments. The Parties agree that such reclassification was not authorized under the Partnership Agreement and that the reclassified amounts shall be restored to CMP\'s distributable profit pool, with such restoration treated as retroactive to the fiscal quarters in which the revenues were originally received by CMP, as follows:
> **(a)** Five Hundred Thirty-Eight Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$538,200) attributable to domestic distribution revenues received in connection with *Salt Wind*, to be restored to the distributable profit pool for the third quarter of calendar year 2020 (Q3 2020); and
> **(b)** Three Hundred Nine Thousand Dollars (\$309,000) attributable to domestic distribution revenues received in connection with *Iron Lullaby*, to be restored to the distributable profit pool for the first quarter of calendar year 2021 (Q1 2021).
**4.2 Accountant Restatement.** Within thirty (30) days following the Effective Date, CMP\'s independent accountant, Clearfield & Moss CPAs, shall restate the applicable waterfall schedules and distribution records for Q3 2020 and Q1 2021 to reflect the restoration of revenues set forth in Section 4.1 above. The restated schedules shall recalculate each partner\'s distributable share for the affected quarters in accordance with the Partnership Agreement as in effect during those periods. To the extent that the restatement results in an adjustment to distributions owed by one Party to the other for the affected periods, any net amount owed to Fonseca shall be credited against the Settlement Amount, and any net amount owed to Rennick shall be offset against his obligation to pay the Settlement Amount. The Parties and their respective counsel shall cooperate in good faith with Clearfield & Moss CPAs to facilitate the timely completion of the restatement contemplated by this Section 4.2.
**5.1 Dual-Signature Requirement.** Section 4.3 of the Partnership Agreement is hereby amended to add the following provision: Any single expenditure, commitment, or disbursement by or on behalf of CMP in an amount exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000.00) shall require the prior written approval of both Fonseca and Rennick. For purposes of this Section 5.1, a \"single expenditure\" shall include any individual payment, invoice, purchase order, contract commitment, or series of related transactions that, in the aggregate, exceed the foregoing threshold. Written approval may be given by email from the approving partner\'s email address of record with CMP, provided that the email expressly references the specific expenditure and the amount thereof. Neither partner shall unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay approval of any expenditure that is consistent with CMP\'s approved annual operating budget and the ordinary course of CMP\'s business.
**5.4 Independent Accountant.** Clearfield & Moss CPAs (Howard Moss, CPA, Partner-in-Charge; 9100 Sunset Boulevard, Suite 220, West Hollywood, California 90069) shall continue to serve as CMP\'s independent accountant for purposes of the quarterly financial reporting required by Section 5.2 and the annual audit required by Section 5.3. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the annual audits for calendar years 2023 and 2024 shall be subject to the oversight and review of Tillerman Forensic Advisory LLC (Greta Sørensen, CPA, CFF, Principal; 350 South Grand Avenue, Suite 1480, Los Angeles, California 90071). Tillerman\'s oversight role shall include, without limitation, the right to: (a) review Clearfield & Moss\'s audit workpapers, methodologies, and conclusions; (b) conduct independent testing of selected account balances and transactions; (c) communicate directly with Clearfield & Moss regarding audit findings; and (d) issue a supplemental report to both partners summarizing its oversight activities and any concerns identified. Tillerman\'s fees and expenses for the oversight engagement shall be a CMP partnership expense, provided that such fees and expenses shall not exceed Forty Thousand Dollars (\$40,000) per audit cycle without the prior written consent of both partners. Following the completion of the calendar year 2024 audit oversight engagement, Tillerman\'s oversight role shall terminate unless both partners agree in writing to extend it.
**7.1 Joint Stipulation.** Within five (5) business days following Fonseca\'s receipt of the First Installment, the Parties, through their respective counsel of record, shall execute and file with the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, a Joint Stipulation for Dismissal of the Action (Case No. 23STCV01897), with prejudice, with each side bearing its own attorney\'s fees and costs. The Joint Stipulation shall provide that the Court shall retain jurisdiction over the Parties and the subject matter of this Agreement pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 664.6 for purposes of enforcing the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including without limitation the payment obligations set forth in Section 1 hereof. Counsel for Fonseca shall prepare the initial draft of the Joint Stipulation and circulate it to counsel for the Rennick Parties for review and approval, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
**9.1 General Obligation.** The Parties shall keep strictly confidential the existence and terms of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, and all related negotiations and communications, and shall not disclose such information to any third party, except:
> **(c)** to Ridgeline Commercial Bank (555 West 7th Street, 18th Floor, Los Angeles, California 90014) and its authorized representatives, solely to the extent necessary in connection with CMP\'s existing One Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$1,400,000) revolving credit facility and any renewals, amendments, or refinancings thereof, provided that any such disclosure shall be accompanied by a written request that the recipient maintain the disclosed information in confidence.
> **(b)** Each individual RSV invoice submitted to CMP, regardless of amount, shall be subject to the dual-signature approval requirement set forth in Section 5.1 of this Agreement. No RSV invoice shall be paid by CMP without the prior written approval of both Fonseca and Rennick. For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement applies in addition to, and not in lieu of, the general dual-signature requirement for expenditures exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000) set forth in Section 5.1.

\"**Escrow Agreement**\" means the escrow agreement of even date herewith entered into by and among Solstice, Apex, and the Escrow Agent, governing the deposit, holding, and release of the Lump-Sum Payment.
\"**Lump-Sum Payment**\" means the aggregate sum of Eight Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$8,750,000) payable by Solstice to Apex pursuant to Section 3.1.
\"**Royalty Cap**\" means One Million Eight Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,800,000) per calendar year, as more fully described in Section 3.2(b).
\"**Royalty Floor**\" means Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$500,000) per calendar year, beginning with calendar year 2026, as more fully described in Section 3.2(a).
\"**Tranche 1**\" means Five Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$5,250,000), as more fully described in Section 3.1(a).
\"**Tranche 2**\" means Three Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$3,500,000), as more fully described in Section 3.1(b).
> \(b\) **Financial Capability.** Solstice has the present financial capability and sufficient available resources to make all payments contemplated by this Agreement, including the Lump-Sum Payment and the Running Royalty payments, and does not know of any reason that would prevent or impair Solstice from making such payments when due.
**Section 3.1 --- Lump-Sum Payment.** In partial consideration for the releases granted in Article VII, the license granted in Article IV, and the covenant not to sue set forth in Section 4.2 and Exhibit B, Solstice shall pay to Apex an aggregate lump-sum settlement payment of Eight Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$8,750,000) (the \"**Lump-Sum Payment**\"), payable in two tranches as follows:
> **(a) Tranche 1.** Within ten (10) business days following the Effective Date (and in no event later than June 30, 2025), Solstice shall pay to the Escrow Agent, by wire transfer of immediately available funds in accordance with the wire instructions set forth in the Escrow Agreement, the sum of Five Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$5,250,000) (\"**Tranche 1**\"). Upon confirmation of the receipt of Tranche 1 into the escrow account maintained by the Escrow Agent, the Escrow Agent shall release the Tranche 1 funds to Apex by wire transfer to the bank account designated by Apex in the Escrow Agreement within three (3) business days of deposit. Solstice shall provide Apex with written confirmation of the wire transfer to the Escrow Agent promptly following its initiation.
> **(b) Tranche 2.** On or before September 15, 2025, Solstice shall pay to the Escrow Agent, by wire transfer of immediately available funds in accordance with the wire instructions set forth in the Escrow Agreement, the sum of Three Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$3,500,000) (\"**Tranche 2**\"). Upon confirmation of the receipt of Tranche 2 into the escrow account maintained by the Escrow Agent, the Escrow Agent shall release the Tranche 2 funds to Apex by wire transfer to the bank account designated by Apex in the Escrow Agreement within three (3) business days of deposit. Solstice shall provide Apex with written confirmation of the wire transfer to the Escrow Agent promptly following its initiation.
> **(c) Late Payment.** Any portion of the Lump-Sum Payment or any Running Royalty payment not paid when due shall bear interest from the applicable due date until the date of actual payment at a rate equal to the lesser of (i) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (eighteen percent (18%) per annum) and (ii) the maximum rate of interest permitted by applicable law. The accrual of interest under this Section 3.1(c) shall not limit or waive any other rights or remedies available to Apex, including Apex\'s right to terminate the Patent License Agreement upon a material breach of payment obligations, as set forth in Section 10.2 of this Agreement. Any interest payable hereunder shall be computed on the basis of a 360-day year composed of twelve 30-day months.
**Section 3.2 --- Running Royalty.** Beginning on the Effective Date and continuing for the remaining life of each Licensed Patent (with the last-to-expire Licensed Patent being the \'105 Patent, expiring January 10, 2038), Solstice shall pay to Apex a running royalty equal to three and three-quarters percent (3.75%) of Net Sales of Licensed Products (the \"**Running Royalty**\"), subject to the Royalty Floor and Royalty Cap set forth below.
> **(a) Royalty Floor.** Beginning with calendar year 2026, and for each full calendar year thereafter during the term of this Agreement, the minimum annual Running Royalty payable by Solstice to Apex shall be Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$500,000) (the \"**Royalty Floor**\"). If the aggregate Running Royalty payments actually due and paid with respect to Net Sales for a given calendar year are less than the Royalty Floor, Solstice shall pay the difference between the actual aggregate Running Royalty and the Royalty Floor within thirty (30) days following the end of such calendar year. For the avoidance of doubt, the Royalty Floor shall not apply to the partial calendar year 2025 (i.e., the period from the Effective Date through December 31, 2025), nor to any partial calendar year at the end of the term resulting from the expiration of the last Licensed Patent. The Royalty Floor shall be prorated for any partial calendar year at the end of the term.
> **(b) Royalty Cap.** The maximum aggregate Running Royalty payable by Solstice to Apex in any single calendar year shall not exceed One Million Eight Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,800,000) (the \"**Royalty Cap**\"). Once cumulative Running Royalty payments for a given calendar year reach the Royalty Cap, no further Running Royalty shall be due or payable for the remainder of that calendar year. The Royalty Cap shall be prorated for any partial calendar year at the beginning or end of the term.
> **(d) Royalty Payments.** Running Royalty payments shall be due and payable within forty-five (45) days after the end of each Calendar Quarter, concurrently with the delivery of the corresponding royalty report. All Running Royalty payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated by Apex in writing from time to time. Apex shall provide Solstice with its initial wire instructions within five (5) business days of the Effective Date and shall provide not less than fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice of any change in wire instructions. All Running Royalty payments shall be made in United States Dollars. To the extent any Net Sales are invoiced in a currency other than United States Dollars, such amounts shall be converted to United States Dollars at the average daily exchange rate published by the European Central Bank for the applicable Calendar Quarter.
**Section 3.3 --- Tax Treatment.** The Parties agree and acknowledge that the Lump-Sum Payment constitutes consideration for the settlement and release of all claims in the Action and for the grant of the Patent License Agreement and the Covenant Not to Sue, and that the Running Royalty constitutes license royalties for the use of intellectual property rights. Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all taxes, duties, assessments, and other governmental charges imposed on it in connection with the payments made or received under this Agreement. Solstice shall comply with all applicable withholding tax obligations under United States federal, state, and local tax law and under the laws of Ireland, including any applicable provisions of the Convention between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of Ireland for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (the \"**U.S.-Ireland Tax Treaty**\"). Apex shall reasonably cooperate with Solstice\'s requests for tax documentation, including the execution and delivery of IRS Form W-9 or such other forms as may be reasonably required to establish Apex\'s tax status and to enable Solstice to comply with its withholding obligations. **Section 2.1 --- Payment Amount.** In consideration of the mutual covenants, releases, and agreements set forth in this Agreement, Cascade shall pay to Vantor the Settlement Amount of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents (\$14,750,000.00) in full and final satisfaction of all Released Claims. The Claims Administrator shall perform all settlement administration tasks as set forth in this Agreement, including but not limited to mailing of Notice, processing of Opt-Out requests and Objections, calculating Individual Settlement Payments, establishing and maintaining the Qualified Settlement Fund, issuing settlement checks, performing tax reporting, and maintaining the Settlement Website and toll-free telephone number.
**[SECTION 3 --- SETTLEMENT CONSIDERATION]{.underline}**
**3.1 Gross Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of the Action and all Released Claims, AMA shall cause to be paid, or shall pay, the total, maximum, all-inclusive, and non-reversionary sum of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,750,000.00) (the \"Gross Settlement Amount\" or \"GSA\"). The GSA constitutes the total maximum monetary obligation of AMA under this Settlement and includes all payments described in this Section 3, including without limitation the Net Settlement Fund, Attorneys\' Fees, Litigation Costs, Class Representative Service Awards, Settlement Administration Costs, and the PAGA Payment. AMA shall have no obligation to pay any amount in excess of the GSA, except for the employer\'s share of payroll taxes as set forth in Section 4.4 of this Agreement.
> The total Class Representative Service Awards shall not exceed Thirty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$35,000.00). The Service Awards shall be paid from the GSA and are in addition to any Individual Settlement Payment that the Class Representatives may receive as Participating Class Members. AMA agrees that it will not oppose service award requests up to and including the amounts stated above. The Court\'s determination of the appropriate service awards, including any reduction in the requested amounts, is not a material term or condition of this Settlement and shall not provide a basis for termination of this Agreement. Any reduction in the service awards by the Court below the requested amounts shall be added to the Net Settlement Fund and distributed to Participating Class Members.
> **(e) PAGA Payment.** Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$750,000.00) of the GSA shall be allocated to the PAGA Payment, representing the civil penalties component of the Settlement attributable to PAGA claims asserted in this Action. The PAGA Payment shall be distributed as follows: seventy-five percent (75%) of the PAGA Payment, which equals Five Hundred Sixty-Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$562,500.00), shall be paid to the LWDA; and twenty-five percent (25%) of the PAGA Payment, which equals One Hundred Eighty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$187,500.00), shall be distributed to Aggrieved Employees (i.e., all Participating Class Members who do not opt out of the Settlement Class), pro rata based on the same allocation formula set forth in Section 4.1, in addition to their Individual Settlement Payments from the Net Settlement Fund. The allocation formula for each Participating Class Member\'s Individual Settlement Payment is expressed as follows:
In the event that a Participating Class Member has zero (0) recorded Overtime Hours during the Class Period, such member\'s Individual Settlement Payment shall be calculated based solely on the workweek component (i.e., the overtime component shall be zero for that member, but the member shall still receive a payment based on the workweek component). The Claims Administrator shall apply the foregoing formula to all Participating Class Members and shall prepare a distribution spreadsheet for review by Class Counsel and Defense Counsel prior to the distribution of settlement checks.
**4.2 Data Source.** The Claims Administrator shall calculate Individual Settlement Payments using Workweek Data provided by AMA and/or NovaPay Solutions Inc. (AMA\'s third-party timekeeping vendor). AMA shall provide the Workweek Data to the Claims Administrator within fourteen (14) calendar days of entry of the Preliminary Approval Order. The Workweek Data shall include, for each Settlement Class Member, the following information: (a) full legal name; (b) last known mailing address; (c) Social Security number (or, at a minimum, the last four digits thereof); (d) dates of employment with AMA during the Class Period; (e) the total number of workweeks worked during the Class Period; and (f) the total number of recorded overtime hours worked during the Class Period. AMA represents and warrants that it will provide the Workweek Data in good faith and that such data will be derived from the most accurate and complete records reasonably available to AMA. In the event of any dispute regarding the accuracy of the Workweek Data, the Parties shall meet and confer in good faith to resolve the dispute, and if the dispute cannot be resolved, either Party may seek resolution from the Court.
**4.3 Estimated Average Individual Payment.** Based on the estimated NSF of Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty-One Thousand Five Hundred Twenty-Five Dollars (\$8,251,525.00) and an estimated class size of approximately 1,850 Participating Class Members, the estimated average Individual Settlement Payment is approximately Four Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Dollars (\$4,460.00). Actual Individual Settlement Payments will vary based on each Participating Class Member\'s individual workweeks and overtime hours worked during the Class Period, as well as the total number of Opt-Outs and the final Court-approved deductions from the GSA. Some Participating Class Members may receive more or less than the estimated average depending on their individual circumstances.

> \(a\) **Wage Portion (50%).** Fifty percent (50%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as wages for services rendered, and shall be subject to applicable federal and state income tax withholding and employee-side payroll taxes, including the employee\'s share of FICA (Social Security and Medicare taxes) and applicable state payroll taxes. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form W-2.
> \(b\) **Interest and Penalties Portion (33.33%).** Thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as interest and penalties, which are not subject to withholding but are generally taxable as ordinary income to the recipient. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (or such other form as may be required by applicable tax law at the time of distribution).
> \(c\) **Non-Wage Damages Portion (16.67%).** Sixteen and sixty-seven hundredths percent (16.67%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as non-wage damages, which are not subject to withholding. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (or such other form as may be required by applicable tax law at the time of distribution).
