**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**Effective Date: December 19, 2023**

This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of December 19, 2023 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:

**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation (\"VHG\" or \"Plaintiff\"), with its principal offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129;

**IRONCLAD INDEMNITY CORPORATION**, a Connecticut-domiciled stock insurance company (\"Ironclad\"), with its principal offices at 55 Constitution Boulevard, Hartford, Connecticut 06103;

**PINNACLE SURPLUS LINES INC.**, a Texas-domiciled surplus-lines insurer (\"Pinnacle\"), with its principal offices at 200 Congress Avenue, Suite 1400, Austin, Texas 78701;

**MONTCLAIR ASSURANCE COMPANY**, a New York-domiciled admitted insurance carrier (\"Montclair\"), with its principal offices at 1 Liberty Plaza, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10006; and

**SOVEREIGN RE LTD.**, a Bermuda-domiciled excess carrier (\"Sovereign Re\"), with its principal offices at 14 Front Street, Hamilton HM 11, Bermuda.

VHG, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re are referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS:**

**A.** VHG is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, whose common stock is publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VMRK,\" and which maintains its principal executive offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129. VHG is engaged in the business of owning, operating, and managing luxury resort hotel properties in the State of Florida. As of the Effective Date, VHG\'s portfolio of properties includes, among others, the following three resort hotel properties (collectively, the \"Insured Properties\"):

> \(i\) the Verimark Grand Key Resort, located at Mile Marker 48, Marathon, Florida 33050, a 287-room full-service luxury resort and marina situated in the Florida Keys;
>
> \(ii\) the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, located at 1400 Estero Boulevard, Fort Myers Beach, Florida 33931, a 412-room beachfront hotel and conference center situated on the Gulf Coast of Florida; and
>
> \(iii\) the Verimark Sunset Shores, located at 7200 Gulf Boulevard, St. Pete Beach, Florida 33706, a 194-room boutique luxury hotel and spa situated on the barrier island of St. Pete Beach on the Gulf of Mexico.

**B.** In connection with VHG\'s ownership and operation of the Insured Properties, VHG procured and maintained a layered insurance program consisting of property and business-interruption coverage as follows:

> \(i\) Ironclad is a stock insurance company domiciled in the State of Connecticut and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Ironclad issued to VHG an all-risk property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number IIC-PRP-2022-07541, for the policy period commencing July 1, 2022 and ending July 1, 2023, providing primary coverage with a per-occurrence limit of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) for property damage and business-interruption losses, subject to a deductible of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per occurrence (the \"Primary Policy\").
>
> \(ii\) Pinnacle is a surplus-lines insurer domiciled in the State of Texas and authorized to transact surplus-lines insurance business in the State of Florida. Pinnacle issued to VHG a first excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number PSL-XS1-2022-3390, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Fifteen Million Dollars (\$15,000,000) in coverage in excess of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the Primary Policy (the \"First Excess Policy\").
>
> \(iii\) Montclair is an admitted insurance carrier domiciled in the State of New York and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Montclair issued to VHG a second excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number MAC-XS2-2022-09817, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy and the First Excess Policy (the \"Second Excess Policy\").
>
> \(iv\) Sovereign Re is an excess carrier domiciled in Bermuda and authorized to transact excess insurance business relating to risks situated in the State of Florida. Sovereign Re issued to VHG a third excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number SRL-XS3-2022-5102, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, and the Second Excess Policy (the \"Third Excess Policy\").

The Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, the Second Excess Policy, and the Third Excess Policy are referred to herein collectively as the \"Policies.\" The Policies provide aggregate tower limits of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) above the Five Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$500,000) deductible applicable under the Primary Policy.

**C.** On September 18, 2022, Hurricane Callista, classified by the National Hurricane Center as a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Veltason Hurricane Wind Scale, made landfall in the Lower Florida Keys with maximum sustained winds of approximately 145 miles per hour and produced storm surge inundation of approximately eight (8) to fourteen (14) feet above normal tide levels in Monroe County and approximately six (6) to ten (10) feet above normal tide levels in Lee County. Hurricane Callista caused catastrophic and widespread damage throughout southern Florida, including significant damage to coastal structures, resort properties, marinas, and critical infrastructure along the Florida Keys and the Gulf Coast of southwestern Florida. As a direct and proximate result of Hurricane Callista, the Insured Properties sustained catastrophic property damage and experienced prolonged and severe business interruption, including complete closure of the Grand Key Resort and the Harborview Hotel & Conference Center for extended periods, and partial closure of Sunset Shores (collectively, the \"Hurricane Callista Losses\"). VHG submitted an initial notice of loss to Ironclad, as primary carrier, on September 22, 2022, four days following the landfall of Hurricane Callista. Thereafter, VHG submitted a sworn statement in proof of loss to Ironclad on November 15, 2022, pursuant to the requirements of the Primary Policy, asserting total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) across the Insured Properties.

**D.** On October 12, 2022, Ironclad, through its designated third-party claims administrator, Arbor Claims Services LLC, and its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, issued a reservation of rights letter to VHG with respect to VHG\'s claim for business-interruption losses. On February 3, 2023, Ironclad issued a formal denial of coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim, asserting, among other grounds, that: (i) the Primary Policy contained a named-windstorm sub-limit that capped business-interruption recovery at an amount substantially below VHG\'s claimed losses; (ii) the period of restoration was subject to dispute, and VHG had failed to establish the proper period of restoration for business-interruption coverage; (iii) certain claimed losses were attributable to flood and storm surge, which were subject to a concurrent causation analysis and the flood exclusion in the Primary Policy; and (iv) VHG had failed to adequately mitigate its losses in breach of its duties under the Primary Policy. On February 10, 2023, Pinnacle, through its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, followed Ironclad\'s denial on a follow-form basis and denied coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim to the extent it fell within Pinnacle\'s layer. Montclair and Sovereign Re, through their joint coverage counsel, Delvecchio & Kraus LLP, did not issue formal denials of coverage but reserved all rights under their respective policies, asserting that their excess layers would not be reached based on the application of the named-windstorm sub-limit asserted by Ironclad and Pinnacle.

**E.** On March 1, 2023, VHG filed a multi-count complaint in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, captioned *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corp., Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, assigned to the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge (the \"Litigation\"). In the Litigation, VHG asserted claims for: (i) breach of contract against all four Insurer Parties; (ii) declaratory judgment seeking a judicial determination of coverage rights under the Policies; and (iii) bad faith, including both statutory bad faith under Section 624.155 of the Florida Statutes and common-law bad faith, against all four Insurer Parties. VHG\'s complaint alleged total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000), comprised of approximately Thirty-One Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$31,400,000) attributable to the Verimark Grand Key Resort, approximately Eighteen Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,700,000) attributable to the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, and approximately Nine Million Nine Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$9,900,000) attributable to the Verimark Sunset Shores. On April 15, 2023, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re, through their respective counsel, filed answers and affirmative defenses denying liability and raising numerous defenses to VHG\'s claims. Thereafter, the Parties conducted extensive fact discovery, including the exchange of voluminous documents, written discovery, and depositions of party representatives, including depositions of VHG\'s Chief Executive Officer Marcus Ellsworth, VHG\'s Chief Financial Officer Diane Calder, VHG\'s General Counsel Nathaniel Driscoll, Ironclad\'s Senior Vice President of Claims Victor Haddon, and Arbor Claims Services LLC\'s lead adjuster Denise Whitford. The Parties also conducted expert discovery, including the retention and deposition of forensic accountants, property damage engineers, meteorological experts, and hospitality industry consultants. On November 1, 2023, VHG filed a motion for partial summary judgment on the issue of whether the named-windstorm sub-limit in the Primary Policy applied to business-interruption losses as opposed to property-damage losses only. On November 15, 2023, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re filed a cross-motion for partial summary judgment on the same issue, arguing that the named-windstorm sub-limit applied to both property-damage and business-interruption losses. On November 20, 2023, the Court entered an order referring the Parties to mediation and staying briefing on the cross-motions for partial summary judgment pending the outcome of the mediation.

**F.** On December 4 and December 5, 2023, the Parties participated in a two-day mediation session before the Honorable Richard Mendelson (Ret.) of Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc. in Miami, Florida. All Parties appeared through their respective counsel and authorized corporate representatives with full settlement authority. At the conclusion of the mediation on December 5, 2023, the Parties reached an agreement in principle to resolve all disputes and claims among them, which agreement in principle was memorialized in a binding term sheet executed by all Parties on that date. The Parties subsequently negotiated the terms of this Agreement to memorialize the final and comprehensive terms of their settlement.

**G.** The Parties desire to fully and finally resolve any and all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, disputes, and controversies between and among them arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies, without any admission of liability, fault, or wrongdoing by any Party, and on the terms and conditions set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1** *Defined Terms.* As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

> \(a\) \"Agreement\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits attached hereto, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time in accordance with Section 9.4.
>
> \(b\) \"Claim\" or \"Claims\" means any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, expenses (including, without limitation, attorneys\' fees and costs of litigation), obligations, judgments, liens, debts, and rights of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, liquidated or unliquidated, arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies.
>
> \(c\) \"Effective Date\" means the date on which this Agreement is fully executed by all Parties, which the Parties agree is December 19, 2023.
>
> \(d\) \"Hurricane Callista Losses\" means any and all property damage, business-interruption losses, loss of rents, extra expenses, debris removal costs, increased cost of construction, loss of business income, and all related losses, costs, and expenses sustained or incurred by VHG at or in connection with the Insured Properties arising out of or relating to Hurricane Callista, which made landfall on September 18, 2022, and the aftermath thereof.
>
> \(e\) \"Insured Properties\" has the meaning set forth in Recital A of this Agreement.
>
> \(f\) \"Insurer Parties\" means Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re, together with their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, underwriters, reinsurers, predecessors, successors, and assigns.
>
> \(g\) \"Litigation\" means the action captioned *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corp., Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, pending in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, before the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge.
>
> \(h\) \"Parties\" means VHG and the Insurer Parties, collectively. \"Party\" means any one of them individually.
>
> \(i\) \"Payment Allocation Schedule\" means the schedule setting forth each Insurer Party\'s respective share of the Settlement Amount, attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.
>
> \(j\) \"Policies\" has the meaning set forth in Recital B of this Agreement, and includes the Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, the Second Excess Policy, and the Third Excess Policy, as each such term is defined in Recital B.
>
> \(k\) \"Released Claims\" has the meaning set forth in Article IV of this Agreement.
>
> \(l\) \"Settlement Amount\" means the aggregate sum of Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,300,000.00), payable to VHG by the Insurer Parties in accordance with Article II of this Agreement.
>
> \(m\) \"VHG Parties\" means VHG, together with its parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, predecessors, successors, and assigns.

**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1** *Total Settlement Amount.* In consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, releases, and obligations set forth in this Agreement, and in full and final settlement and resolution of all Claims among the Parties arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies, the Insurer Parties shall pay to VHG the aggregate sum of Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,300,000.00) (the \"Settlement Amount\"). The Parties acknowledge that the Settlement Amount represents approximately 78.83% of VHG\'s total claimed business-interruption losses of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) and reflects a negotiated compromise of disputed claims among all Parties. The Settlement Amount shall be allocated among the Insurer Parties as set forth in the Payment Allocation Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A and in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.

**Section 2.2** *Allocation of Settlement Amount.* The Settlement Amount shall be allocated among the Insurer Parties as follows:

> \(a\) Ironclad Indemnity Corporation shall pay Twenty-Four Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$24,500,000.00);
>
> \(b\) Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. shall pay Twelve Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$12,200,000.00);
>
> \(c\) Montclair Assurance Company shall pay Six Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$6,800,000.00); and
>
> \(d\) Sovereign Re Ltd. shall pay Three Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$3,800,000.00).

The sum of the individual allocations set forth in subsections (a) through (d) above equals the total Settlement Amount of Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,300,000.00). The foregoing allocation represents the Parties\' agreed-upon allocation and shall not be construed as a determination or admission of the amount of coverage owed by any individual Insurer Party under its respective Policy.

**Section 2.3** *Payment Terms.* Each Insurer Party\'s share of the Settlement Amount, as set forth in Section 2.2, shall be paid in a single lump-sum payment by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars within forty-five (45) calendar days of the Effective Date. Given that the Effective Date is December 19, 2023, the payment deadline shall be February 2, 2024 (the \"Payment Deadline\"). All payments shall be made to the Interest on Lawyers\' Trust Account (IOLTA) of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, counsel for VHG, in accordance with wire transfer instructions to be provided separately and in writing by Calderwood & Harkness LLP to counsel for each respective Insurer Party within five (5) business days of the Effective Date. Each Insurer Party shall provide written confirmation to Calderwood & Harkness LLP of the initiation of its wire transfer no later than two (2) business days prior to the Payment Deadline. Each Insurer Party shall be severally, and not jointly, liable for its respective share of the Settlement Amount as set forth in Section 2.2. No Insurer Party shall be liable, in whole or in part, for the payment obligation of any other Insurer Party. The payment by each Insurer Party of its respective share shall fully discharge that Insurer Party\'s financial obligations under this Agreement regardless of whether any other Insurer Party pays or fails to pay its respective share.

**Section 2.4** *Late Payment.* In the event that any Insurer Party fails to remit its respective share of the Settlement Amount on or before the Payment Deadline, the unpaid amount shall bear interest at the rate of twelve percent (12%) per annum, or the maximum rate permitted under applicable Florida law, whichever is less, computed from the day immediately following the Payment Deadline until the date upon which such payment is received in full. The accrual of interest under this Section 2.4 shall not constitute a waiver of any other rights or remedies available to VHG at law or in equity for any Insurer Party\'s failure to timely make payment, including the right to seek specific performance or other equitable relief.

**Section 2.5** *Tax Treatment.* Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations, if any, arising from the settlement or the payments made pursuant to this Agreement. No Party makes any representation or warranty to any other Party regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Amount or any portion thereof. VHG acknowledges and agrees that no Insurer Party, nor any agent, employee, or counsel of any Insurer Party, has provided or is providing any tax advice to VHG with respect to the Settlement Amount or any portion thereof. The Parties agree that VHG will report the Settlement Amount as proceeds from an insurance recovery for business-interruption losses for applicable tax purposes. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed as tax advice, and each Party is encouraged to consult with its own qualified tax advisors regarding the tax treatment of the Settlement Amount.

**[ARTICLE III --- DISMISSAL OF LITIGATION]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1** *Stipulation of Dismissal.* Within ten (10) business days following receipt by VHG (through the trust account of Calderwood & Harkness LLP) of the full Settlement Amount from all Insurer Parties, the Parties shall jointly execute and file a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice of all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and affirmative defenses in the Litigation, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, before the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge. The Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice shall provide for the dismissal of all claims and counterclaims asserted by any Party in the Litigation with prejudice to their re-filing and shall be in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit B, or in such other form as shall be mutually agreed upon by the Parties through their respective counsel.

**Section 3.2** *Costs and Fees.* Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement, each Party shall bear its own costs, expenses, and attorneys\' fees incurred in connection with the Litigation and the negotiation, preparation, and execution of this Agreement. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, VHG\'s engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP as its litigation counsel and the fees, costs, and expenses incurred by VHG in connection therewith are solely VHG\'s responsibility, and no Insurer Party shall bear any liability for any portion of such fees, costs, or expenses.

**Section 3.3** *Withdrawal of Pending Motions.* Upon the filing of the Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice in the Litigation, all pending motions in the Litigation shall be deemed withdrawn and rendered moot, including without limitation: (a) VHG\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment Regarding the Applicability of the Named-Windstorm Sub-Limit to Business-Interruption Losses, filed on November 1, 2023; and (b) the Cross-Motion for Partial Summary Judgment filed by Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re on November 15, 2023. The Parties agree to cooperate in informing the Court that such motions are withdrawn and need not be adjudicated.

**[ARTICLE IV --- MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1** *Release by VHG.* Effective upon VHG\'s receipt of the full Settlement Amount from all Insurer Parties, VHG, on behalf of itself and all VHG Parties, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each and every Insurer Party, and each of their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents (including, without limitation, Arbor Claims Services LLC and its employees, agents, and representatives, including specifically Denise Whitford), underwriters, reinsurers, predecessors, successors, assigns, and legal counsel (including, without limitation, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP and its attorneys Gregory Stanton, Meredith Liang, and Colin Ashford; and Delvecchio & Kraus LLP and its attorneys Patricia Kraus and Raymond Cho), from any and all Claims of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies (collectively, the \"Released Claims\"). This release includes, without limitation, all claims for breach of contract, breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, statutory bad faith under Section 624.155 of the Florida Statutes, common-law bad faith, declaratory judgment, extra-contractual damages, consequential damages, statutory penalties, punitive damages, attorneys\' fees, pre-judgment and post-judgment interest, costs of litigation, and any and all other relief of any kind or nature whatsoever that was or could have been asserted in the Litigation or in any other action or proceeding.

---END---

**JOINT STIPULATION OF DISMISSAL WITH PREJUDICE**

Plaintiff Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (\"VHG\") and Defendants Ironclad Indemnity Corporation (\"Ironclad\"), Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. (\"Pinnacle\"), Montclair Assurance Company (\"Montclair\"), and Sovereign Re Ltd. (\"Sovereign Re\") (collectively, the \"Parties\"), by and through their undersigned counsel, hereby stipulate and agree as follows:

1\. The Parties have reached a full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and disputes at issue in this action.

2\. Pursuant to Florida Rule of Civil Procedure 1.420(a)(1)(B), the Parties hereby stipulate to the dismissal, with prejudice, of all claims asserted by Plaintiff against Defendants, and all counterclaims and affirmative defenses asserted by Defendants against Plaintiff, in this action.

3\. This dismissal is with prejudice to the re-filing of any of the dismissed claims, counterclaims, or cross-claims by any Party.

4\. Each Party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees incurred in connection with this action, except as otherwise agreed among the Parties.

5\. All pending motions in this action, including Plaintiff\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment filed November 1, 2023 and Defendants\' Cross-Motion for Partial Summary Judgment filed November 15, 2023, are hereby withdrawn and deemed moot.

6\. The Court shall retain jurisdiction solely for the purpose of enforcing the terms of the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release entered into by the Parties effective December 19, 2023.

**WHEREFORE**, the Parties respectfully request that the Court enter an order dismissing this action in its entirety, with prejudice, and in accordance with the terms of this Joint Stipulation.

25-**A. Employment Relationship.** Aldrich was employed by AMA in the position of Senior Vice President of Original Content & Executive Producer from September 5, 2017 through October 14, 2022. Aldrich\'s employment with AMA was governed by that certain Employment Agreement dated September 5, 2017, by and between AMA and Aldrich, as amended by that certain First Amendment to Employment Agreement dated August 1, 2020 (collectively, the \"**Employment Agreement**\"). AMA is a wholly owned subsidiary of Aurelius Global Media Group PLC (\"**AGMG**\"), a public limited company organized under the laws of England and Wales (Companies House Registration No. 08412667), whose ordinary shares are listed on the London Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol LSE: AGMG. Throughout Aldrich\'s tenure with AMA, Aldrich reported to AMA\'s President, Jonathan Mercer, and served in a senior leadership capacity with significant responsibilities for the development, production, and oversight of AMA\'s original unscripted and reality television content portfolio.
26-
27:**B. Termination.** AMA terminated Aldrich\'s employment effective October 14, 2022. AMA designated the termination as \"for cause\" pursuant to Section 7.2(b) of the Employment Agreement. AMA\'s stated bases for the \"for cause\" determination were: (i) material violation of AMA\'s Acceptable Use and Confidentiality Policy, including but not limited to the unauthorized transmission of proprietary information --- including show format bibles, pilot development materials, revenue projections, and talent compensation data --- from AMA\'s corporate systems to Aldrich\'s personal email account (galdrich.private@Northgate Software.com) and to a third-party entity, Halcyon Creek Productions LLC; and (ii) insubordination in connection with Aldrich\'s refusal to comply with a direct instruction from AMA\'s President, Jonathan Mercer, regarding the restructuring of certain production team assignments in or about September 2022. Aldrich disputes the \"for cause\" designation in its entirety and contends that the termination was pretextual and retaliatory, undertaken in response to Aldrich\'s internal complaints regarding AMA\'s production practices and budgetary irregularities, and that the cited grounds were manufactured or exaggerated to deprive Aldrich of contractual severance benefits and other entitlements.
28-
29:**C. The Litigation.** On December 9, 2022, Aldrich filed a Complaint against AMA in the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles --- Central District, assigned Case No. 22STCV41087 (the \"**Complaint**\"), asserting claims for: (1) Wrongful Termination in Violation of Public Policy; (2) Breach of Contract; (3) Breach of the Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing; (4) Declaratory Relief regarding the enforceability of restrictive covenant provisions contained in the Employment Agreement under California Business and Professions Code Section 16600; and (5) Violation of California Labor Code Section 2802 (failure to reimburse necessary business expenses). On January 20, 2023, AMA filed a Cross-Complaint against Aldrich (the \"**Cross-Complaint**\") in the same action, asserting claims for: (1) Breach of the Employment Agreement (Sections 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, and 9.4); (2) Misappropriation of Trade Secrets pursuant to the California Uniform Trade Secrets Act, California Civil Code Section 3426 *et seq.* (\"**CUTSA**\"); (3) Breach of Fiduciary Duty; and (4) Conversion. In the Litigation, Aldrich is represented by Whitfield & Associates (Cameron Whitfield, Principal; Julia Nazarian, Associate), with offices at 9465 Wilshire Boulevard, Suite 320, Beverly Hills, California 90212. AMA is represented by Calderwood & Harkness LLP (Renata Vasquez, Partner; Devon Archer, Senior Associate), with offices at 777 South Flower Street, Suite 4200, Los Angeles, California 90017. The Parties have engaged in extensive discovery in the Litigation, including the exchange of written discovery, the production of documents, and the deposition of multiple fact witnesses.
30-
31-**D. Mediation.** The Parties participated in a full-day mediation session on December 8, 2023, before the Honorable Patricia Okoro (Ret.) of Westpark Dispute Resolution Inc., located at 1925 Century Park East, Suite 1700, Los Angeles, California 90067. The Parties reached agreement on the material terms set forth herein during and following said mediation, and the mediator\'s proposal was accepted by both Parties on December 12, 2023. The Parties thereafter negotiated the specific terms and provisions of this Agreement through their respective counsel.
--
33-**E. Restrictive Covenant Provisions.** The Employment Agreement contains restrictive covenant provisions in Section 9, including: Section 9.1 (Non-Competition, prohibiting Aldrich from working for any \"Competing Enterprise\" for a period of eighteen (18) months following termination); Section 9.2 (Non-Solicitation of Employees, prohibiting Aldrich from soliciting AMA employees for a period of twenty-four (24) months following termination); Section 9.3 (Non-Solicitation of Business Relationships, prohibiting Aldrich from soliciting AMA\'s network, platform, and advertiser clients for a period of twenty-four (24) months following termination); and Section 9.4 (Confidentiality, imposing an indefinite obligation of non-disclosure with respect to Confidential Information). These provisions are collectively referred to herein as the \"**Restrictive Covenant Provisions**.\" Aldrich contends that Section 9.1 is void and unenforceable under California Business and Professions Code Section 16600 and related California case law. The Parties desire to modify certain of the Restrictive Covenant Provisions as part of this Agreement, as more particularly described in Section 6 hereof.
34-
35:**F. Equity Awards.** During his employment with AMA, Aldrich was granted a total of forty-two thousand five hundred (42,500) restricted stock units (\"**RSUs**\") of AGMG common shares, pursuant to AGMG\'s equity compensation plan and the applicable award agreements. As of Aldrich\'s termination date of October 14, 2022, fifteen thousand three hundred (15,300) RSUs remained unvested, subject to the terms of the applicable award agreements and the equity compensation plan. The Parties desire to resolve the treatment of Aldrich\'s unvested RSUs as part of this Agreement, as more particularly described in Section 3 hereof.
36-
37-**G. Desire to Resolve.** The Parties desire to fully, finally, and completely resolve all claims, disputes, and controversies between them, including without limitation all claims and cross-claims asserted in the Litigation (Case No. 22STCV41087), all disputes relating to Aldrich\'s employment with AMA and the termination thereof, and all disputes relating to the Employment Agreement and the Restrictive Covenant Provisions, without admission of liability, wrongdoing, or fault by either Party. This Agreement is a compromise of disputed claims and shall not be construed as an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or fault by either Party.
38-

The Settlement Payment shall be made within twenty-one (21) calendar days following the Effective Date (and, for the avoidance of doubt, following the expiration of the Revocation Period described in Section 13 without revocation by Aldrich). Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated by Aldrich in writing, pursuant to the wire transfer instructions to be provided by Aldrich to AMA\'s counsel (Calderwood & Harkness LLP, attention Renata Vasquez) within five (5) business days of the Effective Date, in the form attached hereto as **Exhibit A** (or in such other form as AMA may reasonably require). The Settlement Payment shall be in full and complete satisfaction of all claims, demands, and causes of action of any kind or nature whatsoever that Aldrich has or may have against AMA or any of the AMA Released Parties arising from, relating to, or in any way connected with Aldrich\'s employment with AMA, the termination of such employment, the Employment Agreement, and the Litigation.

This portion of the Settlement Payment shall be reported by AMA on IRS Form W-2 (or the applicable equivalent) for tax year 2024.

This portion of the Settlement Payment shall be reported by AMA on IRS Form 1099-MISC (or the applicable equivalent) for tax year 2024.

Neither Party shall take a position on any tax return or in any tax proceeding that is inconsistent with the allocation set forth herein, unless required to do so by a final determination of a court of competent jurisdiction or by a settlement with a taxing authority.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Settlement Payment is inclusive of and intended to encompass any and all amounts that might otherwise be owed, claimed, or due to Aldrich, including without limitation:
88-
89-> \(i\) Severance benefits under Section 7.3 of the Employment Agreement, which would have provided for a lump-sum severance payment of Nine Hundred Seventy Thousand Dollars (\$970,000.00), representing twenty-four (24) months of Aldrich\'s base salary of Four Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$485,000.00) per year, had Aldrich been terminated without cause;
--

AMA makes no representations or warranties regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Payment or any portion thereof, and Aldrich acknowledges and agrees that he has been advised to consult with, and has had the opportunity to consult with, his own independent tax advisor regarding the federal, state, and local tax consequences of the Settlement Payment and this Agreement. Aldrich acknowledges that AMA has not provided him with any tax advice in connection with this Agreement and that AMA shall not be liable for any tax consequences to Aldrich arising from the Settlement Payment or any other consideration provided under this Agreement.

**[MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**

**[PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT]{.underline}**

**TO:** Elaine Forsythe, Responsible Partner Howard Bellamy, Billing Partner

**FROM:** Tiffany Rosenthal, Lead Associate

**DATE:** January 3, 2024

**RE:** Confirmation of Receipt of Settlement Funds --- *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corporation, Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547 (Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, Miami-Dade County)

**MATTER/ENGAGEMENT NO.:** 1021-00003

**CLIENT:** Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (Nasdaq: VMRK)

**[I. Purpose of Memorandum]{.underline}**

The purpose of this memorandum is to confirm that all settlement payments due under the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release dated December 19, 2023 (the \"Settlement Agreement\") have been received in full and have cleared into the Calderwood & Harkness LLP client trust account maintained at our Miami office. This memorandum is intended to serve as the firm\'s contemporaneous internal record documenting receipt of the settlement proceeds and to outline the remaining steps necessary to conclude this engagement.

As background, the Settlement Agreement resolved all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and potential claims asserted in *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corporation, Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, pending before the Honorable Catherine Embry in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County. The underlying dispute concerned the defendants\' denial and underpayment of a substantial business-interruption insurance claim submitted by Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (\"VHG\" or the \"Client\") arising from hurricane damage sustained at multiple hotel and resort properties during the 2022 hurricane season.

The total aggregate settlement amount is **\$47,300,000.00** (Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars and 00/100). All four insurer defendants --- Ironclad Indemnity Corporation (\"Ironclad\"), Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. (\"Pinnacle\"), Montclair Assurance Company (\"Montclair\"), and Sovereign Re Ltd. (\"Sovereign Re\") --- have funded their respective shares of the settlement in accordance with the Payment Allocation Schedule set forth in Exhibit A to the Settlement Agreement. Each wire transfer has been received and has fully cleared through the firm\'s trust account, and no amounts remain outstanding from any settling party. As detailed below, all payments were received well in advance of the contractual payment deadline.

**[II. Settlement Agreement Reference]{.underline}**

The definitive Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release was executed on December 19, 2023, by all parties to the litigation --- VHG as plaintiff, and Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re as defendants --- as well as by their respective counsel of record. The Settlement Agreement memorialized the terms previously agreed upon in the Term Sheet executed on December 5, 2023, during a two-day mediation session conducted before the Honorable Richard Mendelson (Ret.) at Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc. in Miami, Florida.

Section 3.1 of the Settlement Agreement obligated the four insurer defendants to make lump-sum payment of their respective settlement shares within forty-five (45) calendar days following execution of the Settlement Agreement, establishing a contractual payment deadline of **February 2, 2024**. As described more fully below, all four payments were received and cleared no later than January 2, 2024 --- a full thirty-one (31) days in advance of the contractual deadline.

The specific allocation of the aggregate settlement amount among the four insurer defendants was governed by Exhibit A to the Settlement Agreement (the \"Payment Allocation Schedule\"), which set forth each insurer\'s pro rata share based on the applicable insurance tower layer. The Payment Allocation Schedule was negotiated during the mediation and reflected a layered allocation roughly proportional to each insurer\'s exposure within the insurance program, with the primary carrier bearing the largest share and the upper-layer excess carriers bearing progressively smaller shares. The precise allocation is detailed in Section III below.

The Settlement Agreement also contains a mutual release of all claims (Section 4), a confidentiality provision governing the settlement amount (Section 7), representations and warranties of authority (Section 5), and a provision requiring the parties to file a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice within thirty (30) days of receipt of all settlement payments (Section 6). The status of the stipulation of dismissal is addressed in Section VI.B below.

**[III. Summary of Funds Received]{.underline}**

**A. Table of Wire Receipts**

The following table sets forth the details of the four wire transfers received from the settling defendants, including the paying party, applicable policy number, layer position, settlement amount, wire initiation date, date funds cleared, and the identity of sending counsel:

  Ironclad Indemnity Corporation   IIC-PRP-2022-07541   Primary (\$25M limit, \$500K per-occurrence deductible)   \$24,500,000.00         December 28, 2023         December 29, 2023        Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP (Gregory Stanton)

  Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc.      PSL-XS1-2022-3390    1st Excess (\$15M xs \$25M)                               \$12,200,000.00         December 28, 2023         December 29, 2023        Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP (Gregory Stanton)

  Montclair Assurance Company      MAC-XS2-2022-09817   2nd Excess (\$10M xs \$40M)                               \$6,800,000.00          December 29, 2023         January 2, 2024          Delvecchio & Kraus LLP (Patricia Kraus)

  Sovereign Re Ltd.                SRL-XS3-2022-5102    3rd Excess (\$10M xs \$50M)                               \$3,800,000.00          December 29, 2023         January 2, 2024          Delvecchio & Kraus LLP (Patricia Kraus)

The total funds received across all four wire transfers are calculated as follows:

> \$24,500,000.00 (Ironclad Indemnity Corporation) + \$12,200,000.00 (Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc.) + \$6,800,000.00 (Montclair Assurance Company) + \$3,800,000.00 (Sovereign Re Ltd.) = **\$47,300,000.00 (Total)**

**[IV. Wire Transfer Details]{.underline}**

**A. Ironclad and Pinnacle Payments**

Wire instructions for the Calderwood & Harkness LLP client trust account were transmitted to Gregory Stanton of Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP via letter dated December 20, 2023. That letter was prepared by the undersigned and included the firm\'s full wire routing information, ABA routing number, beneficiary account details, and reference information identifying the matter and applicable Settlement Agreement section. A copy of the wire instruction letter is included as part of **Attachment 3** to this memorandum.

Ironclad Indemnity Corporation\'s payment of **\$24,500,000.00** and Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc.\'s payment of **\$12,200,000.00** were each wired separately on **December 28, 2023**. Both wires were initiated through the same sending institution, which is consistent with the fact that Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP served as joint defense counsel for both Ironclad and Pinnacle in this matter. Both transfers were confirmed as fully cleared and available in the Calderwood & Harkness client trust account on **December 29, 2023**, the next business day.

The combined payment received from Ironclad and Pinnacle totals **\$36,700,000.00**, representing approximately 77.6% of the total aggregate settlement.

It bears noting that Ironclad\'s settlement payment of \$24,500,000.00 represents its full primary policy layer limit of \$25,000,000.00 less the \$500,000.00 per-occurrence deductible that is retained by VHG under the terms of Policy No. IIC-PRP-2022-07541. The deductible was not at issue in the litigation and was not a component of the settlement, as VHG had already absorbed the deductible amount. Accordingly, Ironclad\'s payment of \$24,500,000.00 effectively constitutes a settlement at 100% of its net exposure under the primary layer, exclusive of the deductible.

**B. Montclair and Sovereign Re Payments**

Wire instructions for the Calderwood & Harkness LLP client trust account were separately transmitted to Patricia Kraus of Delvecchio & Kraus LLP via letter also dated December 20, 2023, prepared by the undersigned. Montclair Assurance Company\'s payment of **\$6,800,000.00** and Sovereign Re Ltd.\'s payment of **\$3,800,000.00** were each wired separately on **December 29, 2023**. The combined payment received from Montclair and Sovereign Re totals **\$10,600,000.00**, representing approximately 22.4% of the total aggregate settlement.

I confirmed receipt of all four wires directly with our firm\'s trust account administrator, Daniel Carrillo, on the morning of January 2, 2024, and obtained copies of the bank wire confirmation receipts at that time. >

>

The descending recovery percentages across the insurance tower are consistent with the settlement dynamics observed during the mediation. The upper-layer excess carriers obtained progressively steeper discounts commensurate with the increasing uncertainty as to whether VHG\'s total provable loss would fully penetrate each successive layer. In particular, Sovereign Re\'s position at the \$50 million excess attachment point afforded it significant leverage given the disputed quantum of VHG\'s business-interruption losses in the range above \$50 million.

All amounts set forth in the Settlement Agreement and received via wire transfer match the Payment Allocation Schedule set forth in Exhibit A to the Settlement Agreement. A copy of Exhibit A is included as **Attachment 2** to this memorandum.

{"file_path":"response.md","content":"# Largest litigation settlement

## Answer

The largest **litigation settlement** in the materials is **$47,300,000** in **_Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corporation, Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd._, Case No. 2022-CA-031547**, in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, Miami-Dade County.

This was the Hurricane Callista property/business-interruption insurance coverage litigation. Verimark asserted approximately **$60 million** in business-interruption losses. The insurers agreed to pay **$47.3 million**—approximately 78.83% of the claimed loss—to resolve the litigation.

## Why $47.3 million is the correct number

The definitive **Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release**, effective December 19, 2023, expressly defines the aggregate “Settlement Amount” as **$47,300,000** and then confirms in Section 2.1 that the insurers must pay that amount in full and final settlement of the claims. It is allocated as follows:

| Paying insurer | Settlement share |
|---|---:|
| Ironclad Indemnity Corporation | $24,500,000 |
| Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. | $12,200,000 |
| Montclair Assurance Company | $6,800,000 |
| Sovereign Re Ltd. | $3,800,000 |
| **Total** | **$47,300,000** |

The allocation reconciles exactly: $24.5 million + $12.2 million + $6.8 million + $3.8 million = **$47.3 million**. The agreement also provides for mutual releases and dismissal with prejudice, confirming that this was a completed litigation resolution rather than merely a demand, offer, or settlement authority figure.

The firm’s post-settlement funds memorandum confirms that all four wires were received and cleared, with no amount outstanding. Accordingly, the $47.3 million was not merely an agreed-in-principle figure; it was funded under the executed agreement.

## Documents relied on

1. **`documents/matters/1021-00003/Mediation & Settlement/settlement-agreement-mutual-release.docx`**
   - Effective Date: December 19, 2023.
   - Recital E identifies the underlying Verimark litigation and Case No. 2022-CA-031547.
   - Section 1.1(l) defines “Settlement Amount” as **$47,300,000**.
   - Section 2.1 states that the insurers shall pay the aggregate $47.3 million in full and final settlement.
   - Section 2.2 and Exhibit A contain the four-insurer allocation shown above.
   - Section 3.1 provides for dismissal with prejudice after receipt of the settlement.

2. **`documents/matters/1021-00003/Mediation & Settlement/term-sheet-mediated-settlement.docx`**
   - Marked as executed at the December 4–5, 2023 mediation.
   - Section 1.1 likewise states an aggregate settlement amount of **$47,300,000** and Section 1.2 gives the same allocation.
   - I treated the term sheet and the definitive agreement as documents for the **same settlement**, not two separate settlements, so the amount was counted once.

3. **`documents/matters/1021-00003/Post-Settlement & Closing/confirmation-receipt-settlement-funds-memo.docx`**
   - Confirms that the definitive agreement was executed by all parties and that all four settlement payments were received and cleared.
   - Reconciles the four wires to the same **$47,300,000** aggregate.

## Comparison and treatment of other figures

I used the amount expressly defined in each final/executed settlement instrument—not the claimant’s demand, the alleged damages, the policy limits, a draft, a term sheet counted separately, or a settlement-authority ceiling. For comparison, other executed litigation settlement documents in the collection define amounts such as $14.75 million, $9.75 million, $8.75 million, $7.85 million, and $4.5 million, all below $47.3 million.

There is one important scope distinction. Matter **1018-00009** contains an executed IRS Form 906 Closing Agreement stating a **$47.6 million agreed adjustment to taxable income** and **$10 million of additional federal income tax**. That is a tax-administration compromise, not a payment labeled as a litigation “Settlement Amount,” and the matter was an IRS examination/Appeals proceeding rather than the litigated action used for litigation credentials. I therefore did not present the $47.6 million taxable-income adjustment as a litigation settlement. On the litigation-settlement basis requested, the defensible lead credential is:

> **$47.3 million settlement in the Verimark Hospitality Group Hurricane Callista insurance coverage litigation (Matter 1021-00003).**
"}

lines.text: # Largest litigation settlement
## Answer

The largest **litigation settlement** in the materials is **$47,300,000** in **_Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corporation, Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd._, Case No. 2022-CA-031547**, in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, Miami-Dade County.

This was the Hurricane Callista property/business-interruption insurance coverage litigation. Verimark asserted approximately **$60 million** in business-interruption losses. The insurers agreed to pay **$47.3 million**—approximately 78.83% of the claimed loss—to resolve the litigation.
## Why $47.3 million is the correct number

The definitive **Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release**, effective December 19, 2023, expressly defines the aggregate “Settlement Amount” as **$47,300,000** and then confirms in Section 2.1 that the insurers must pay that amount in full and final settlement of the claims. It is allocated as follows:
| Paying insurer | Settlement share |
| Ironclad Indemnity Corporation | $24,500,000 |
| Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. | $12,200,000 |
| Montclair Assurance Company | $6,800,000 |
| Sovereign Re Ltd. | $3,800,000 |

The allocation reconciles exactly: $24.5 million + $12.2 million + $6.8 million + $3.8 million = **$47.3 million**. The agreement also provides for mutual releases and dismissal with prejudice, confirming that this was a completed litigation resolution rather than merely a demand, offer, or settlement authority figure.

The firm’s post-settlement funds memorandum confirms that all four wires were received and cleared, with no amount outstanding. Accordingly, the $47.3 million was not merely an agreed-in-principle figure; it was funded under the executed agreement.
## Documents relied on
1. **`documents/matters/1021-00003/Mediation & Settlement/settlement-agreement-mutual-release.docx`**
- Effective Date: December 19, 2023.
- Recital E identifies the underlying Verimark litigation and Case No. 2022-CA-031547.
- Section 1.1(l) defines “Settlement Amount” as **$47,300,000**.
- Section 2.1 states that the insurers shall pay the aggregate $47.3 million in full and final settlement.
- Section 2.2 and Exhibit A contain the four-insurer allocation shown above.
- Section 3.1 provides for dismissal with prejudice after receipt of the settlement.
2. **`documents/matters/1021-00003/Mediation & Settlement/term-sheet-mediated-settlement.docx`**
- Marked as executed at the December 4–5, 2023 mediation.
- Section 1.1 likewise states an aggregate settlement amount of **$47,300,000** and Section 1.2 gives the same allocation.
- I treated the term sheet and the definitive agreement as documents for the **same settlement**, not two separate settlements, so the amount was counted once.
3. **`documents/matters/1021-00003/Post-Settlement & Closing/confirmation-receipt-settlement-funds-memo.docx`**
- Confirms that the definitive agreement was executed by all parties and that all four settlement payments were received and cleared.
- Reconciles the four wires to the same **$47,300,000** aggregate.
## Comparison and treatment of other figures

I used the amount expressly defined in each final/executed settlement instrument—not the claimant’s demand, the alleged damages, the policy limits, a draft, a term sheet counted separately, or a settlement-authority ceiling. For comparison, other executed litigation settlement documents in the collection define amounts such as $14.75 million, $9.75 million, $8.75 million, $7.85 million, and $4.5 million, all below $47.3 million.

There is one important scope distinction. Matter **1018-00009** contains an executed IRS Form 906 Closing Agreement stating a **$47.6 million agreed adjustment to taxable income** and **$10 million of additional federal income tax**. That is a tax-administration compromise, not a payment labeled as a litigation “Settlement Amount,” and the matter was an IRS examination/Appeals proceeding rather than the litigated action used for litigation credentials. I therefore did not present the $47.6 million taxable-income adjustment as a litigation settlement. On the litigation-settlement basis requested, the defensible lead credential is:
> **$47.3 million settlement in the Verimark Hospitality Group Hurricane Callista insurance coverage litigation (Matter 1021-00003).**
